rect.data-content:
Lab A: functional tests
Selected Hub/LMS services.
Approved test data and dependencies.
Readiness checks before QA starts.

Lab B: load or resilience tests
Selected product and test profile.
Isolation suited to the test impact.
Agreed resource and duration bounds.

Lab C: rapid POC
Approved subset or alternate setup.
Track deviations from the baseline.
Named owner and an expiry policy.

Choose isolation to match the test
Compare a lab in shared infrastructure with a dedicated project/cluster and data services.
Agree network, identity, state, test data and shared dependencies; a namespace alone may not meet every test need.

g.textArea: Expected outcomes
Manifest fields to agree
Controls and lifecycle

rect.data-content:
• Repeat a test against identifiable versions.
• Support different testing needs in parallel.
• Exercise provisioning and recreation from code.

• Service images and infrastructure-template version.
• Settings, dependencies, schema and test-data profile.
• Owner, purpose, size, expiry and acceptance checks.
• References to secrets; no secret values in the manifest.

• Scope execution access to the owned lab.
• Bound sizing, concurrency and allowed duration.
• Keep evidence, then verify managed cleanup.
• Assign failed-provisioning and cleanup ownership.

Infrastructure, deployment and QA are separate handoffs
Terraform provisions the approved target; the chosen app deployment path installs the selected release and test setup. Readiness checks precede QA tests.
Use Proposal 01 apply controls; consume approved artifacts from 03/04. Repository consolidation is not a prerequisite. Production promotion remains a separate release decision.

g.textArea: Basis: Nov 12 proposal discussion; environment/runtime snapshots Nov 2–3, 2026. Lab profiles, manifest, instances, controls and self-service automation are proposed.

g.data-frame: 05B QA lab: request, provision, test and clean up

rect.data-title: 05B QA lab: request, provision, test and clean up

g.textArea: 05B QA lab: request, provision, test and clean up
QA / automation / approvers / DevOps | Draft | Follow the numbered handoffs; request ownership, readiness and cleanup evidence stay with each instance.
Blue = proposed | Gray = saved evidence or context | Yellow = gate, exception or team decision
QA requests / feedback
Provisioning / approvals
Apps / readiness
QA tests / evidence
Lifecycle / DevOps

rect.data-content:
1. Select what to test [QA]
Choose a release manifest and lab profile.
Provide purpose, owner and requested lifetime.
Submit through the agreed interface.

Incomplete or unauthorized request
Return clear findings to QA; do not provision.
Correct inputs or obtain the required approval.

Provisioning failed or only partly completed
Do not start testing or assume automatic rollback.
DevOps reconciles the owned resources and state.
Record recovery or cleanup actions.

2. Validate the request [Automation]
Check profile, versions, access and limits.
Allocate an instance ID and ownership scope.
Confirm any required request approval.

3. Review the final target plan
Select lab inputs and isolated state scope.
Authorize execution under the agreed policy.
Apply controls: 01B (review or approved policy).

4. Provision infrastructure [Automation]
A scoped executor runs Terraform for this lab.
Verify resources and capture required outputs.
Stop on failed or partial apply.

5. Deploy the selected release [Automation]
Deploy manifest versions and required dependencies.
Apply the agreed test schema and seed approved data.
Application deployment is separate from Terraform apply.

6. Check lab readiness [Automation]
Verify settings, access and dependencies.
Match release versions and check health.
Hand over only a ready instance to QA.

Lab is not ready: hold QA testing
Return deployment/readiness diagnostics.
Assigned owners correct the setup.
Repeat the readiness checks.

7. Run the selected tests [QA]
Use the manifest and instance ID.
Execute functional, load, recovery or POC tests.
Record failures as well as passes.

8. Save results and evidence [QA / Automation]
Record manifest, instance, versions and test outcomes.
Separate product defects from environment failures.
Retain agreed evidence before removing the lab.

Completion or expiry starts the agreed lifecycle policy
Track the owner, expiry, retention and any approved extension.
Keep shared/protected dependencies outside this lab’s teardown scope.
If cleanup fails, assign follow-up and track residual resources and cost.

9. Remove only the owned lab [Automation]
Stop/remove its deployment desired state.
Authorize and run target cleanup under the agreed policy.
Verify owned resources and record any residue.
Retain the agreed evidence and closure record.

g.textArea: Proposed workflow, not an existing QA provisioning service. Interface, approvals, deployment engine, test data, isolation and expiry/cleanup policy require team agreement.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: QA + DevOps
Evidence before expanding
Dependencies and integration work
Operating controls to agree
Open design decisions

rect.data-content:
• Recreate the selected infrastructure and release versions.
• Prove readiness, test-data setup and selected QA journeys.
• Exercise overlapping requests and failed/partial operations.
• Verify owned-resource cleanup and record any residue.

• Reviewed infrastructure modules, inputs, state and identities.
• Artifact access, app deployment path and dependency setup.
• Schema/seed fixtures, secret references and test identities.
• Evidence storage, cost visibility and cleanup reconciliation.

• Approved sizing, quotas, concurrency and allowed duration.
• Synthetic or explicitly approved sanitized test data.
• Per-instance ownership and scoped execution/cleanup.
• Expiry, extensions, evidence retention and failure support.

• Shared infrastructure or dedicated project/cluster per need?
• Which dependencies are shared versus owned by each lab?
• Workflow/button or direct CLI, and who authorizes execution?
• Which profiles, tests, counts and lifecycle rules are required?

Keep the handoffs and claims explicit
Provisioning exercises infrastructure code; it does not by itself prove production disaster recovery. Choose recovery tests against agreed criteria.
Consume approved artifacts from 03/04, use 01 execution controls, and coordinate release policy with 11. Existing shared environments are context; no new lab count or date is committed.

g.textArea: Basis: Nov 12 meeting intent and saved environment/Terraform/GitOps explanations. Infrastructure coverage, current access, QA data policy and operation owners must be confirmed before implementation.
